where: blaze-profile: adding a table to the history (crates/blaze-profile/src/history.rs, schema.rs)
what: Adding the one table `accounts` took eleven hand edits that nothing ties together: `schema::TABLES`' length (`[&Table; 30]`), a field of `History`, its initialiser in `open`, a method, the batch in `write`, the fixed-size `tables: [(..); 22]`, a `done(..)` clear, a field of `Flushed` and its line in the one literal that names every field, a view in views.sql and a section in docs/profiling.md.
cost: about twenty minutes of reading to find the sites, written without a compiler (write-only lane), so a missed one is a round trip through the runner
cause: each fact table is spelled out by hand at every stage of a flush
whys: why eleven edits: a flush names each table's rows, batch, count and clear separately
why separately: the fact tables are plain Vec fields of History, not values of one trait the flush iterates
property: a table is a convention across a file, not a type
class: one concept spelled at many sites by hand (one-concept-one-home)
prevention: not built: a `Fact` trait (rows -> batches by bytes, its table, its count) and one list of fact buffers the flush iterates, so a new table is one impl and one schema const
workaround: grep history.rs for `schema::MISSES` and `misses` and mirror every hit
